html:
The Yuracaré are an Indigenous people of the forested foothills where the Andes meet the Amazon lowlands in central Bolivia, in the Chapare and along rivers flowing to the Mamoré. Their language is an isolate.

They lived as hunters, fishers and slash-and-burn farmers, moving often. They stayed outside the Inca Empire, whose frontier ran along the mountains above them. In the late 1700s Franciscan missionaries founded missions among them, with mixed success, and in the 1900s settlers and coca farmers moved into the Chapare. Some live today in the Isiboro Sécure park, shared with the Mojeño. Neighbours to the north-west included the Tacana.
